content: 1. Dexlansoprazole is indicated for the healing of all grades of erosive esophagitis (EE) and for maintaining the healing of EE. For healing, the recommended dose is 60 mg orally once daily for up to 8 weeks. For maintenance, the recommended dose is 30 mg orally once daily for up to 6 months. 2. Dexlansoprazole is also indicated for the treatment of heartburn associated with symptomatic non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). The recommended dose is 30 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks. 3. Concomitant use of dexlansoprazole with erlotinib is contraindicated. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) like dexlansoprazole can decrease the solubility and bioavailability of erlotinib by altering the pH of the upper gastrointestinal tract. This interaction may reduce the efficacy of erlotinib. 4. Dexlansoprazole increases the systemic exposure of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided with mavacamten. 5. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This coadministration is contraindicated as it may result in a loss of virologic response and the development of resistance. The mechanism may involve CYP2C19 inhibition and reduced gastric pH, leading to decreased nelfinavir absorption. 6. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or the development of resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 7. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as acalabrutinib solubility decreases with increasing gastric pH. Dose separation may not eliminate the interaction due to the long-lasting effect of PPIs. 8. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP2C19 inducer, can lower the exposure of CYP2C19 substrates. 9. Apalutamide also decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers like apalutamide can reduce the exposure of CYP3A4 substrates. 10. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 11. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of itraconazole and ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the dose of lonafarnib or continue at the starting dose. 15. Dexlansoprazole decreases the effects of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and sustained-release dosage forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nilotinib solubility is pH-dependent, and separating doses may not eliminate the interaction due to the extended duration of PPI action. 17. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider using short-acting antacids instead of PPIs or H2 antagonists. 18. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use H2-receptor antagonists or antacids if needed, and administer pexidartinib at least 2 hours before or 10 hours after taking an H2-receptor antagonist. 19. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, making it practically insoluble at pH >5. 20. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of clopidogrel by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clopidogrel efficacy may be reduced by drugs that inhibit CYP2C19, as its antiplatelet activity depends on its active metabolite. 21. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 22. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when coadministered with cannabidiol. 23. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of capecitabine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Elevated gastric pH caused by PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and/or reduce absorption. 24. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 25. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 26. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of bosutinib by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. PPIs may decrease bosutinib concentration by approximately 45%, as bosutinib displays pH-dependent solubility. 27. Dexlansoprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and coadministration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution. 28. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of tazemetostat by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
